question: Is our closed-form AM implementation faithful to the AM paper (target, beta/mass-matching, key handling), and is AM designed for acquiring new content at all or only for compacting content already in the cache?
variable_under_test: none (literature read + code read, no GPU)
baseline_ref: AM.pdf = arXiv 2602.16284v2 'Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching'; code baseline = canonical AM config EXP-001 (KEY_MODE=freeze, ENABLE_BETA unset, TOP_T=64, per_document)

diagnostics.paper: Zweiger, Fu, Guo, Kim — Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching, arXiv 2602.16284v2 (ICML 2026), 29pp, read in full via pdftotext -layout
paper_sections_used: C.2 linear algebra + Alg 3 NNLS + Stabilizing beta

paper_numbers.l2_reg_on_beta_and_cv: degraded performance for ALL positive lambda

our_divergences.what: apply_document_am_write_to_cache never reads config.target_mode; only apply_am_update_to_cache (:168-186) does, and that is reachable only via legacy_decoupled (:672-676). execution_mode default 'per_document' (:64).
our_divergences.consequence: TARGET_MODE was a dead env var in every results.csv run; EXP-008's bit-identical outcome is a no-op, so HYP-T1's NULL does not test the target.

our_divergences.what: max_queries_per_head=64 with no env knob; paper uses 16k-50k per KV-head.
our_divergences.consequence: per-head design matrix X is 64x64 at top_t=64 (exactly determined) and 64x128 at top_t=128 (underdetermined; core.py:198-204 min-norm branch). Explains the unexplained EXP-007 top128 regression (MT 2.686).

our_divergences.what: reference queries come from prefilling MT synthesis conversations against the cartridge; the document is not in context. Paper always prefills on the source text (repeat-/context-prefill/self-study). No on-policy layer-sequential re-extraction (finetune.py:359-579 writes all layers from one pre-write bank).
our_divergences.consequence: Qref is off-distribution w.r.t. the content being written.

our_divergences.what: KEY_MODE=freeze has no counterpart in the paper (Ck is always a subset of the compacted block's own keys) AND it silently disables beta, since _should_fit_beta returns key_mode != 'freeze'.
our_divergences.consequence: the canonical config runs AM with neither Ck selection nor mass matching - the paper's weakest ablation.

our_divergences.what: no upper bound on w (paper: e^3 / e^7); lower bound 1e-12 => beta floor -27.63 (paper: -3, prune at -7); n_iters=200 (paper: 2 or 0); torch.linalg.lstsq warm start with default gels driver returns NaN/Inf silently on rank-deficient Phi and the `except RuntimeError` never fires; residual-target formulation `(target-fixed_mass).clamp_min(1e-12)` at :215 has no counterpart in the paper and can zero the entire NNLS target.
our_divergences.consequence: NaN inside the fit (EXP-006), finite max|beta|~66-68 under the sibling tree (EXP-005), and all-zero value-solve design matrix -> core.py:230 NaN (EXP-005b).

our_divergences.what: NNLS refit at every greedy step with 200 PGD iters (paper Alg.2: k=4 keys/step, refit every tau=2, iters=0); (Phi^T r).abs() instead of the signed r^T Phi_:,j of Alg.1 line 5; no beta<-7 prune / w<=e^7 cap; rewrite_keys_on_support discards the selector's beta (:259, :270) and refits it separately at finetune.py:514, breaking the joint (Ck,beta) fit.
our_divergences.consequence: KEY_MODE=omp as written is ~100x more expensive than the paper's variant and is not the paper's AM-OMP.

our_divergences.what: residual formulation over a 64-of-512 subset of columns vs the paper's joint solve over all t rows of Cv.
our_divergences.consequence: a continual adaptation, not an error, but it means the fitted object is not the paper's Cv.

command: pdftotext -layout AM.pdf /tmp/AM.txt ; read cartridges/am/{finetune,value_solve,core,key_select,query_accum,reference_data,teacher,continual}.py and examples/qasper2/train/continual_am_sparse.py ; edited research_loop/state/literature_ledger.md (append-only, 8 LIT entries). NO source code modified, no GPU used.
observations: Q1 — WHAT THE VALUE-SOLVE FITS. AM fits (Ck, beta, Cv) so that a compacted block reproduces TWO quantities of the block it was derived from, per KV-head and per layer, over reference queries Qref: (1) the LOCALLY NORMALISED attention output Attn(q;Ck,beta,Cv) = softmax(qCk^T/sqrt(d)+beta) Cv ~= Attn(q;K,V) = softmax(qK^T/sqrt(d)) V, and (2) the UNNORMALISED attention mass Mass(q;Ck,beta) = sum_j exp(q(Ck)_j^T/sqrt(d)+beta_j) ~= Mass(q;K) = sum_{k=1..T} exp(qK_k^T/sqrt(d)). App. A.2 gives the reason: attention over [block ; K_fixed] is a mixture of the two blocks' local outputs weighted by their masses, so matching output AND mass makes the compacted block behave correctly under concatenation with ANY future tokens. Cv is then ordinary least squares Cv* = argmin ||X Cv - Y||_F^2 = (X^T X)^-1 X^T Y with Y_i = Attn(q_i;K,V) and X_i = softmax(q_i Ck^T/sqrt(d)+beta), solved per layer per KV-head in FP32 via torch.linalg.lstsq. Qref comes from prefilling the model ON THE VERY TEXT BEING COMPACTED: repeat-prefill ('{C} Repeat the previous context. {C}', queries taken while reconstructing C), context-prefill (prefill C alone), and self-study (4 fixed prompts, LM(.|C,a), all query vectors recorded during prefill+decode), reservoir-sampled to AT MOST 50,000 queries per KV-head (avg ~16,000 on QuALITY). Optionally on-policy: layers are compacted sequentially and Qref for layer l is re-extracted with layers <l already compacted. Q2 — DOES OUR IMPLEMENTATION MATCH IT. Partly, with five concrete divergences. (a) B-WIRE CONFIRMED AS A BUG: apply_document_am_write_to_cache (cartridges/am/finetune.py:337-595) never reads config.target_mode; it unconditionally builds the teacher target at finetune.py:477 from [cartridge || doc] KV. target_mode is only consumed by apply_am_update_to_cache (finetune.py:168-186), reachable solely from the legacy_decoupled path (finetune.py:672-676). execution_mode defaults to 'per_document' (finetune.py:64) and the launcher's AM_EXECUTION_MODE also defaults to per_document, so TARGET_MODE was a dead env var in every run in results.csv. EXP-008's bit-identical result is a no-op, not a null. (b) REFERENCE-QUERY SCALE: finetune.py:81 max_queries_per_head=64, applied at finetune.py:425-427; there is NO env knob for it in examples/qasper2/train/continual_am_sparse.py, so every experiment solved with n=64 queries per head against t=top_t columns. At top_t=64 the system X is 64x64 (exactly determined -> interpolation); at top_t=128 it is 64x128 (underdetermined -> core.py:198-204 min-norm branch). The paper uses n=16k-50k with t~100. (c) QUERY SOURCE: continual.py:172-182 / finetune.py:291-334 extract queries by prefilling the MT SYNTHESIS CONVERSATIONS against the current cartridge; the document text is not in context. The paper's queries always come from a model that has read the source text. No on-policy layer-sequential re-extraction (all layers written from one pre-write query bank, finetune.py:359-579). (d) NO Ck SELECTION AND NO beta IN THE CANONICAL CONFIG: key_mode defaults to 'freeze' (finetune.py:69) and _should_fit_beta (finetune.py:256-261) returns key_mode != 'freeze', so ENABLE_BETA unset + KEY_MODE=freeze disables BOTH of AM's components; only Cv is fitted, on a fixed 64-slot support. The paper has no frozen-key variant. (e) SOLVE SCOPE: value_solve.py:67-121 uses a residual formulation (fix the 448 non-selected values, solve the selected columns of the full-cache softmax) - a defensible continual adaptation, but the paper solves all t rows of Cv jointly. Faithful parts: the softmax is over the full cache with 1/sqrt(d) scaling and an additive beta bias (core.py:76-111); targets are locally normalised attention outputs pre-o_proj (teacher.py:134-154, query_accum.py:239-249); FP32 solve; log-sum-exp mass (teacher.py:157-177). Q3 — BETA / MASS MATCHING, LINE BY LINE. Paper: parameterise w_j = exp(beta_j) > 0 and solve min_{w>=0} ||A w - m||_2^2 with A_ij = exp(q_i (Ck)_j^T/sqrt(d)) and m_i = sum_{k=1..T} exp(q_i K_k^T/sqrt(d)), over ALL t compacted keys against the FULL mass; then beta = log w. Algorithm 3: init from unconstrained lstsq, clamp to >= eps, THEN clamp to <= u, return immediately if iters=0, else estimate L ~ ||M||_2^2 by power iteration, step 1/L, and run `iters` projected gradient steps re-projecting into [eps,u] each step. Safeguards: Highest-Attention keys use a BOUNDED least squares with e^-3 <= w <= e^3 (beta in [-3,3]) and iters=2; OMP keys use iters=0, cap w <= e^7, and PRUNE any selected key with beta < -7, continuing selection until all retained keys satisfy beta >= -7. Stated failure mode: 'once beta is very negative, the corresponding key cannot contribute to the attention output, regardless of Cv'. Everything is FP32; the paper also reports that l2 regularisation on the beta/Cv solves degraded performance for every positive lambda. Ours (key_select.py:13-48, 165-224): NO UPPER BOUND anywhere - clamp is min-only at :46; the lower bound is 1e-12, so beta floors at log(1e-12) ~= -27.63 (:97, :160, :219), 9x more negative than the paper's own -3 and past its -7 prune threshold; n_iters=200 (:96/:145/:159/:172) vs the paper's 2 or 0; the warm start at :35 is torch.linalg.lstsq with the DEFAULT gels driver, which on CUDA gives undefined (NaN/Inf) output for rank-deficient inputs WITHOUT raising, so the `except RuntimeError` at :36 never fires and NaN then survives every clamp (torch.clamp passes NaN through - which is exactly why EXP-006's output clamp could not repair it); and refit_beta_nnls fits only the SELECTED slots against a residual target `(target - fixed_mass).clamp_min(1e-12)` (:215), a formulation absent from the paper, which drives the whole NNLS target to 1e-12 (hence w->0, beta->-27.6, then an all-zero design matrix X in the value solve and the EXP-005b 'NaNs in ridge lstsq solution' at core.py:230) whenever the 448 untouched slots already supply more mass than the teacher target. beta_fit_scope defaults to 'selected' (finetune.py:71). The 64x64 shape of Phi (LIT-003) is what makes the rank-deficient gels warm start likely. Q4 — IS AM DESIGNED FOR ACQUIRING NEW CONTENT. No. AM is defined only as compaction of content already present in the cache: Ck is restricted to be a SUBSET OF THE ORIGINAL KEYS of the block being compacted (Sec 3.3, Ck = K_{S,:}), and beta/Cv are then fit so that block reproduces ITS OWN attention behaviour. The values solved for therefore sit on keys that already route correctly for that content - Fig. 5's 'no learned values' ablation (keep the original V_S) still 'yields a reasonable approximation', which only makes sense when the keys came from the same text. The paper contains no procedure for writing content into keys fitted to different content, and names our regime as OPEN: 'a promising direction is to move away from subset selection for Ck (e.g. directly optimizing compact keys)' and 'architectures or training procedures that ... explicitly operate over a fixed set of keys and values' (Sec 6, Future work). On frozen vs re-selected keys the paper is explicit in the only multi-shot setting it has, App. F.3 online compaction: it compacts 'the entire context except for the most recent 20 tokens', INCLUDING previously compacted portions, and states it did so 'rather than, for example, freezing previously compacted portions'. Sec 3.5/App. C.3 chunked compaction concatenates per-chunk compacted segments and never overwrites one chunk's slots with another chunk's content. Bearing on B-ROUTE: App. A.2 'Why biases matter' states that with Ck a subset of K and no bias, Mass(q;Ck) <= Mass(q;K) for every q, so the compacted block 'systematically receives too little global weight' under concatenation with future tokens - i.e. the paper's own account of the frozen-key routing deficit, and beta is its designed remedy. Our canonical config runs with beta disabled and keys frozen, so it has neither AM's key-selection nor AM's mass correction.
